lines.Shunichi: Suggests looking at the bank statements.
lines.Takumi: Suggests looking at the ledger of outgoings.

periods.public: Participants share their findings. They debate the tension between ease of administration, the cost of fixed overheads, and the psychological impact of payment timing on attendance.

lines.Asuka: Mentions that non-joiners dislike large upfront costs.
lines.Benjamin: Points out that chasing small payments is a nightmare for the treasurer.
lines.Jonathan: Notes that a small group does all the work and attendance.
lines.Shunichi: Observes that charging per event reduced weekday turnout.
lines.Takumi: Highlights that most costs are fixed regardless of attendance.

lines.Asuka: Questions if a flexible system would be too complex.
lines.Benjamin: Agrees that complexity hurts the person managing the books.
lines.Jonathan: Asks if the heavy users should pay more.
lines.Shunichi: Argues that making people pay every time creates a barrier to entry.
lines.Takumi: Warns that the club cannot afford to lose guaranteed income.

lines.Asuka: Notes that visibility of payment levels might alienate some.
lines.Benjamin: Suggests a balance between simplicity and fairness.
lines.Jonathan: Points out the unfairness of the current distribution.
lines.Shunichi: Emphasizes the need for a welcoming atmosphere.
lines.Takumi: Insists on a predictable revenue stream.

periods.public: The committee evaluates the three proposed structures against the gathered evidence. They weigh the risk of administrative burnout against the risk of member attrition.

lines.Asuka: Argues for the lowest barrier to entry for newcomers.
lines.Benjamin: Argues for the lowest administrative burden.
lines.Jonathan: Argues for a system that reflects actual usage.
lines.Shunichi: Argues for a system that encourages regular attendance.
lines.Takumi: Argues for the most secure financial foundation.

lines.Asuka: Questions if the treasurer can handle per-event fees.
lines.Benjamin: Confirms that per-event fees are the worst option for the treasurer.
lines.Jonathan: Suggests that a middle ground might satisfy the heavy users.
lines.Shunichi: Warns that any per-event cost will kill the weekday vibe.
lines.Takumi: Points out that fixed costs must be covered first.

lines.Asuka: Admits the administrative risk is high.
lines.Benjamin: Pushes for the simplest possible collection method.
lines.Jonathan: Considers the impact on the core group of volunteers.
lines.Shunichi: Agrees that a single payment removes the hesitation to attend.
lines.Takumi: Supports the most predictable income model.

seats.Takumi: Wants financial predictability and coverage of fixed costs. He argues from a position of stability and resists guesswork.
seats.Benjamin: Wants to minimize the treasurer's workload. He uses logic to argue against complex collection methods.
seats.Jonathan: Wants fairness regarding attendance and effort. He advocates for a system that recognizes different levels of use.
seats.Shunichi: Wants to remove psychological barriers to attendance. He focuses on the atmosphere and the habit of coming to the club.
seats.Asuka: Wants to keep the club accessible to newcomers. She argues for low entry barriers and privacy regarding contributions.
